gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-questrial: Cut-stencil swagger up top: Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve terminals, while Questrial below keeps its lines flat and single-weight. Made small, the heading would lose some of that bite.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-radio-canada: Structural from the first glance, Stencilia leaves spacious curve gaps while Radio Canada draws plain sans lines with no pressure variation. The sharpest thing here is the pull between stencil bite and quiet lines.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-readex-pro: Striking, with spacious gaps at its curve terminals, Stencilia tells the eye where to look. Readex Pro follows with broad terminal gaps and horizontals matching its verticals, so text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-roboto: Roboto keeps capitals and lowercase close in height, with generous round mouths. Stencilia handles the loud work of grabbing attention, while Roboto handles the quiet work of carrying text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-saira: Sharp and structured: Stencilia opens its curve terminals wide, while Saira rounds its letters up toward the top line. But the real draw is a loud heading and a clean body that never compete.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-sarpanch: Striking and structural, Stencilia leaves wide gaps at its curve terminals. Sarpanch, with its clearly open lowercase e, makes long paragraphs feel approachable and unhurried rather than heavy from start to finish.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-sen: Stencil cuts meet tall, rounded lowercase: Stencilia gives the structure while Sen draws its curves at constant weight. Sen then keeps every curve as sturdy as its straights, a modern foil to the stencil bite.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-sofia-sans: Striking is Stencilia, all spacious gaps at the curve terminals. Sofia Sans, with no stroke modulation and tall rounded lowercase like cut acrylic, should read smoothly across many lines.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-tiktok-sans: Striking and structural, Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve terminals. TikTok Sans lifts its x-height close to cap height and opens the c wide, a modern partner for the heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans has big lowercase eyes and tubular strokes. Stencilia supplies the structure, so what stands out most is stencil bite beside a sign-painter's single-stroke softness at constant width.
